newsitem.title: USA: Ciampi denies France, others, don't want lira in EMU.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi denies France, others, don't want lira in EMU.

text.p: Italy's Treasury and Budget Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi denied Monday that France or other countries were against Italy joining a single European currency.
"No one wants Italy out of the euro," Ciampi told reporters.
Ciampi, who is attending the IMF and World Bank annual meetings, added that "at this occasion we have furthered our relations with our main partners.
"Yesterday we had an excellent meeting with (the French finance minister Jean) Arthuis, which has been an extremely positive anticipation of the upcoming Naples' (bilateral) meeting."
Ciampi also criticized reporters for suggesting that French Prime Minister Jacques Chirac might be against Italy's participation in the euro on stability grounds.
"Chirac said exactly the opposite," Ciampi said when asked about press reports to that effect.
"Chirac said that a united Europe will make it possible to avoid situations such as those that have affected France recently...," Ciampi said.
Journalists were citing reports that Chirac had blamed the lira, rather than the Far East producers, for the difficult situation in the French textile industry.

Ciampi also dismissed reports of a statement by Italy's Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco, who said that "ten days ago the main European partners suddenly speeeded up their effort towards meeting the Maastricht criteria on convergence, linking this to the desire, wish and hope that Italy may be excluded."
Visco had said that "obviously there were no official statements over this. We simply became aware that something was changing, over the last 10 days."
